verifiedByCode: The 250th admitted distinct height is scheduled before intakeAbort; intakeAbort is separate from blockScanRuntimeAbort, so ordinary close does not abort the tail pass.

Post-close heads never call blockscan schedule; main also suppresses noteHead once closed, preventing 251 from arming producer or polluting its source hint. Duplicate known heights may still emit reorg/duplicate evidence without consuming the count.

Public mempool callbacks check intake abort before queue admission and before publishing pending execution evidence. inFlight and evidenceWork counters cover previously started local firehose reads/evidence jobs and are joined before generator completion.
Disabled hint stream wakes directly on intake abort. Filtered/firehose sockets close on intake abort and their close handlers wake a currently empty intake queue.
Production scheduler remains the execution owner. Bounded lifecycle joins scheduler plus coarse pricing producers/successors, then observes next head only for timing before normal shutdown.
With no head bound, head observation still schedules through the existing latest-head scheduler, no new dispatch lane or success filtering.
limits: Independent source review only; author tests and build results not rerun here.
A stalled/missing next real head leaves the observer waiting; an external owned-process watchdog may stop it and retain an interrupted result, never restart/extend the sample silently.

Filtered/firehose empty queue wake currently relies on WebSocket close event. This is valid for the real transport, but a direct abort wake would remove close-handshake latency; this is an improvement suggestion, not a proven deadlock.
Observed height gaps are retained as gap events and cannot count as successful work or full continuous coverage.
recommendation: Proceed after author production-body generator/drain tests and build pass; freeze actual integrated hashes and inspect final 250-tail drain/251 observation evidence.
